A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PM-KVQ research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched reliably across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning and coding evaluations, quantization ablations, and transformer-block sensitivity analyses in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds throughput measurements, instruction-following evaluations, additional comparisons, and implementation-cost analyses.

M1.justification: v2 adds an evaluated PM-KVQ plus QuestAttention combination, extending inference to sparse attention (Appendix C.6, Table 10). The core progressive quantization schedule, Equivalent Right Shift, sensitivity-based allocation, positional-interpolation calibration and Section 3 pipeline remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds IFEval instruction following with short outputs, substantially extending coverage beyond competition mathematics and code generation (Appendix C.2, Table 6). Existing evaluation and calibration datasets are retained. Changing CMIMC-2025 to CMIMC-2024 in the setup prose aligns it with the existing Table 2 label rather than establishing a dataset replacement.

E2.justification: The original Table 2 comparators are retained. v2 additionally evaluates KVTuner for mixed-precision reasoning accuracy (Table 8), QuestAttention as the control for combined sparse attention and quantization (Table 10), and QServe for calibration time (Table 11). This substantially broadens the evaluated comparison methods and controls.

E3.justification: New protocols include A100-80G throughput measurements at 16K/24K/32K output lengths with different feasible batch sizes, memory-triggered truncation of higher-bit KIVI, and additional memory/bit-width configurations. IFEval introduces strict/loose prompt and instruction metrics with one response per prompt. MiKV's preserved cache is described as BF16 instead of FP16, a reported setting revision that does not establish rerunning the retained results.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of throughput versus output length, higher-bit KIVI under memory limits, hardware-memory sensitivity, sparse-attention compatibility, preparation overhead, and response-length distributions (Section 4.3; Appendices C.3 and C.5–C.8). The original shrinking and interpolation ablations and block-sensitivity analyses are retained; moving Figure 3 into the main text is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains its existing plus/minus reporting unchanged. Neither version supplies explicit seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or additional experiment-level repetition information. The new tables use point estimates, a practice already present in v1's ablations.

E6.justification: Table 2 and the original ablation tables retain identical numerical results. Substantial new results include throughput of 2.73–5.18 times the original 16-bit models, IFEval scores, and KVTuner comparisons: AIME-2024 pass@1 is 40.21 for PM-KVQ versus 34.17 for KVTuner. Tables 7 and 9–12 add memory-constrained accuracy, sparse-attention results, calibration timing and response-length counts.

T1.justification: Appendix D introduces Theorem D.1 and a detailed quotient-and-remainder proof of Equivalent Right Shift, whereas v1 states the equivalence without proof. This adds substantive formal reasoning for the existing formula. However, the new proof contains an incorrect inequality in Equation (25).

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion add a principal claim of 2.73–5.18 times higher throughput than the original 16-bit models. This expands the claimed contribution from accuracy under memory constraints to measured inference acceleration. The original methodological contributions and up-to-8% accuracy claim are retained.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of the accuracy–throughput tradeoff, memory-constrained comparisons, short-output applicability and sparse-attention compatibility. Appendix C.8 explains different benefits for short responses and long responses whose early tokens use higher precision. Section 4.4.3 explicitly qualifies aggressive interpolation scaling. The original limitations remain essentially unchanged in Appendix E.

D1.justification: v2 documents using KIVI's inference engine and 2/4-bit CUDA kernels, alongside newly implemented 8/16-bit and shrinking kernels. It also discloses BF16 model weights, OpenCompass scoring, KVTuner quantization settings, throughput configurations and preparation times. These substantially improve implementation documentation. Both versions advertise the same code repository.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to KVTuner, Quest, IFEval and OpenCompass and connects them to the additional evaluations. The original related-work coverage and central positioning remain largely intact. The switch from numbered to author–year citations does not itself change research positioning.

P1.justification: The main narrative remains recognizable, with localized shortening, wording corrections and expanded explanations. Small-model sensitivity discussion moves into the main ablations; Broader Impacts becomes an Ethics Statement, and reproducibility and LLM-use statements are added. The conference header and author-role note also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds a throughput table and seven appendix tables, substantially expanding the visual presentation of evidence. Existing ablation tables are renumbered, Figure 3 moves into the main text, and Figure 2 is relocated. The original figures retain their graphical content, while conference typography, headings and page layout replace the preprint styling.

improvement.justification: v1 evaluates accuracy through fake quantization but lacks measured deployment efficiency. v2 substantially addresses that gap with CUDA-based throughput measurements and preparation costs, while KVTuner and memory-limited KIVI comparisons strengthen evaluation of the central memory-allocation approach. It also exposes the throughput cost relative to KIVI rather than presenting acceleration alone. The local proof error in Equation (25) and unchanged limitations text need correction, but do not outweigh these substantial empirical and reproducibility gains.
